9_1.headline: Write the cryptography policy
9_1.teaser: Where you encrypt, and who keeps the keys.
missed: The recovery key of an encrypted disk does not belong on the same device. The IT-Grundschutz of Germany's BSI requires long-lived keys to be kept offline, outside the systems in use (CON.1.A2).
An encrypted backup only helps while the key exists. If the key is lost with the server, so is the backup. The IT-Grundschutz requires encrypted data to stay accessible over long periods (CON.1.A2).
Certificates expire. When your website's certificate has expired, browsers warn your visitors. The IT-Grundschutz requires time-limited certificates to be renewed in time (CON.1.A4).

learn.title: Where you encrypt, and who holds the keys
body: Encryption protects data where it can slip out of your hands: on a lost laptop, on its way across the internet, in a backup kept off site. Without the key, nobody can read it.

Two things record it: your list of accepted methods, and the cryptography policy, which says where you encrypt and how you handle keys and certificates, such as your website's, and prints the list. Which methods count as secure is set out in Technical Guideline TR-02102, which Germany's BSI updates every year.
learn.duty: The law requires policies and procedures for the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption. It does not say which methods; the measures take the state of the art into account.

list.title: Your accepted methods
list.lead: The methods your company uses for encryption, signatures and secure connections, and the ones it no longer uses. Until you keep a list of your own, this is what Germany's BSI recommends in TR-02102; your policy on the next screen prints it.

status.deprecated: Only for what exists, not for anything new

list.change: Change single entries on the requirement page

konzept.title: Your cryptography policy
konzept.lead: The template has fixed sections on methods, keys and responsibility, and your company's name is already in it. Read it, then add below where you encrypt. Whoever looks after your IT can tell you what is already set up.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
sections.text: This policy sets out how {company} uses encryption and other cryptographic methods, so that unauthorised people can neither read information nor change it unnoticed. It applies to all devices, software and services the company works with, including those a service provider runs for us.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text:
We use only established methods and currently recommended key lengths with no known vulnerabilities. When we buy devices, software or services, we make sure they use such methods. Our list of methods:
{acceptedCrypto}

sections.heading: Keys and certificates
sections.text: We keep secret keys and recovery keys where unauthorised people cannot reach them, and apart from the devices they unlock. We renew certificates, such as our website's, before they expire. If a key has fallen into the wrong hands, or we suspect it has, we replace it. We securely delete keys we no longer need.

sections.heading: Responsibility
sections.text: Management decides who implements this policy and who manages keys and certificates. Where a service provider runs systems for us, we agree with them that they follow this policy. Everyone who sets up or looks after encrypted systems knows it.

sections.heading: Review
sections.text: We review this policy regularly. If a method we use becomes known to be insecure, we secure it or replace it.

clauses.label: TR-02102 as the benchmark
clauses.heading: Benchmark
clauses.text: Which methods and key lengths count as secure we take from Technical Guideline TR-02102 of Germany's BSI, in its current version.

clauses.label: Laptops
clauses.heading: Laptops
clauses.text: The disks of all laptops are encrypted.

clauses.label: Work phones and tablets
clauses.heading: Work phones and tablets
clauses.text: Work phones and tablets are protected by a screen lock, and their storage is encrypted.

clauses.label: USB sticks
clauses.heading: USB sticks and external drives
clauses.text: Anyone who takes company data along on a USB stick or an external drive encrypts it.

clauses.label: Backups
clauses.heading: Backups
clauses.text: Backups kept off site or with a service provider are encrypted. We keep the key separately, so that we can still read the backup after an outage.

clauses.label: Website and remote access
clauses.heading: Website and remote access
clauses.text: Our website and remote access to our systems can be reached only over encrypted connections.

clauses.label: Confidential email
clauses.heading: Confidential email
clauses.text: We send especially confidential content by email only when it is encrypted so that only the recipient can read it, for example with S/MIME or PGP.

clauses.label: Annual review
clauses.heading: Annual review
clauses.text: At least once a year we check whether the methods and key lengths we use are still secure enough.

clauses.label: Quantum-safe methods
clauses.heading: Quantum-safe methods
clauses.text: For data that must stay confidential for many years, we plan the move to quantum-safe methods following the BSI's recommendations.

done.title: Your cryptography policy is written
done.note: Give it to everyone who sets up your devices and services, including your IT service provider.
